narratives.name: Orchestrating Strategic Delivery Through Coordinated Programme Governance
narratives.description: How coordinated programme governance enables integrated strategic delivery across multiple projects.

narrativeContexts.context: Organizations pursue strategic objectives that require coordinated delivery across multiple interdependent projects, where individual project management cannot achieve the integrated capabilities and benefits that justify the programme investment.

The programme must establish governance that balances strategic oversight with team autonomy, structure delivery through progressive tranches, and ensure cross-project coordination produces integrated results rather than fragmented outputs.

Programme leadership defines governance frameworks with distributed decision authority, sequences delivery into capability-releasing tranches with exit criteria, and implements dependency management processes that make cross-project interactions transparent and resolvable.

The programme delivers integrated strategic capabilities through coordinated multi-project delivery, with governance providing reliable assurance and dependency management enabling predictable flow across project boundaries.

citationNames: The Standard for Program Management, 4th Edition

narratives.name: Programme Coordination and Governance Overview
narratives.description: Practice overview describing the coordination and governance approach for programme delivery.

narrativeContexts.context: Programmes managing multiple interdependent projects face two fundamental coordination challenges: invisible dependencies that cascade across project boundaries, and monolithic delivery that overwhelms organizational change capacity. Without structured governance and delivery sequencing, programmes devolve into collections of independent projects that fail to deliver integrated strategic value.

The programme establishes governance frameworks that balance strategic oversight with team autonomy, structures delivery into progressive tranches that match delivery pace to organizational absorption capacity, and systematically manages cross-project dependencies through proactive identification, analysis, and structural reduction. MSP's tranche model, SAFe's programme boards, and Flight Levels' decision architecture converge on a coordination approach that makes dependencies transparent, sequences delivery into manageable waves, and distributes decision authority across strategic, coordination, and operational levels.

narratives.name: Sequencing Strategic Value Through Tranche-Based Delivery Planning
narratives.description: How the roadmap sequences strategic value delivery through progressive tranches.

narrativeContexts.context: Programmes must deliver complex strategic capabilities through coordinated multi-project delivery, and the roadmap structures this delivery into progressive tranches that release coherent capability increments aligned with benefit realization milestones.

Roadmaps face constant pressure from changing strategy, emerging dependencies, and the gap between the rate of delivery and the organization's capacity to absorb change, requiring active adaptation rather than rigid plan adherence.

The roadmap is treated as an adaptive strategic instrument with tranche boundaries, exit criteria, and learning objectives that enable data-driven replanning while maintaining strategic direction and benefit realization trajectory.

narratives.name: Establishing Decision Architecture for Programme Assurance
narratives.description: How distributed decision architecture enables effective programme governance and assurance.

narrativeContexts.context: Programme governance is designed with distributed decision authority across strategic, coordination, and operational levels, defining governance bodies, reporting cadence, escalation paths, and stage gate criteria that balance oversight with team autonomy.

Governance bodies operate at mandated cadence, conducting reviews that assess strategic alignment, benefit realization, risk posture, and cross-project coordination effectiveness using data-driven metrics rather than status reports alone.

Governance effectiveness is periodically assessed through self-evaluation or independent review, measuring whether governance decisions are timely, well-informed, and proportionate in overhead to the assurance value they provide.
Governance processes are refined based on effectiveness assessments, with practices documented as organizational standards and decision architecture adapted as the programme matures through tranches.

narratives.name: From Invisible Blockers to Predictive Dependency Orchestration
narratives.description: How dependency management evolves from reactive tracking to predictive orchestration.

narrativeContexts.context: Programme teams work on interdependent projects where invisible dependencies create surprise blockers, cascade delays, and integration failures that undermine coordinated delivery.

The programme commits to making dependencies transparent through systematic identification, visual boards, and structured coordination events that surface the hidden web of cross-project interactions.

Managing dependencies at scale reveals deeply entangled project structures requiring structural changes to team topologies, architectural decoupling, and shifts from component teams to feature teams to fundamentally reduce dependency density.

The programme achieves predictive dependency management where historical patterns inform proactive identification, automated tracking reduces overhead, and teams independently manage routine dependencies as an organizational practice.

narratives.name: Delivering Strategic Change Through Progressive Capability Waves
narratives.description: How tranches structure progressive delivery that balances ambition with organizational absorption capacity.

narrativeContexts.context: Programmes that attempt to deliver all strategic capabilities simultaneously overwhelm organizational change capacity, creating resistance, integration failures, and benefit realization gaps that undermine the programme investment thesis.

Delivery must be structured into progressive tranches that release coherent capability increments, each sized to balance the rate of delivery with the organization's capacity to absorb, adopt, and sustain change.

Each tranche is scoped with exit criteria and learning objectives, mobilized with resources and coordination mechanisms, executed with governance oversight, and reviewed against benefit targets before capabilities are transitioned to operational ownership.

The programme delivers integrated strategic value through manageable waves of change, with each tranche building on lessons learned and enabling data-driven decisions about programme continuation, adaptation, or closure.

narratives.description: How the dependency register evolves from basic catalogue to predictive tracking instrument.

narrativeContexts.context: Programme teams identify and catalogue dependencies using programme boards, tracking tools, and planning events to create a shared understanding of cross-project interactions.

The dependency register evolves from a basic catalogue through risk-assessed and actively tracked states to a predictive instrument that uses historical patterns to anticipate and prevent dependencies before they materialize.

narratives.name: Planning Delivery Waves That Balance Ambition with Absorption Capacity
narratives.description: How tranche plans balance delivery ambition with organizational change absorption capacity.

narrativeContexts.context: Each tranche plan outlines scope, constituent projects, exit criteria, and resources, designed to deliver a coherent capability increment while respecting the organization's capacity to absorb change.
The plan is executed with coordinated project delivery, dependency management, and organizational change activities operating in parallel to produce integrated results.
Tranche progress is tracked against milestones and benefit targets, with decision gates providing governance authorities objective bases for continuation, adaptation, or closure decisions.
Post-tranche review captures lessons learned, evaluates exit criteria achievement, and feeds insights into future tranche planning to improve delivery effectiveness across the programme lifecycle.

narratives.name: Designing Governance That Enables Speed While Assuring Strategic Value
narratives.description: How the governance framework balances control with enablement across programme levels.

narrativeContexts.context: Programmes require governance that provides strategic assurance and decision-making authority while avoiding bureaucratic overhead that impedes delivery speed and team autonomy.
The governance framework must define decision rights, reporting cadence, escalation paths, and stage gates that balance control with enablement across strategic, coordination, and operational levels.

Governance evolves from principled authority structures through structured mechanisms to data-driven operating models that use programme metrics, trend analysis, and benefit tracking to inform decisions.
The programme achieves lightweight governance that provides reliable assurance to organizational leadership, with practices documented as organizational standards for reuse in future programmes.

activities.name: Map and Resolve Cross-Project Dependencies
activities.description: Systematically identify, visualize, and resolve dependencies between programme projects.

narratives.name: Surfacing and Resolving the Hidden Web of Project Interdependencies
narratives.description: How to systematically identify, visualize, and resolve cross-project dependencies.

narrativeContexts.context: Dependency management requires that the programme has identified its constituent projects and established coordination mechanisms such as programme boards, dependency tracking tools, and cross-team planning events.

Teams identify and classify dependencies during programme increment planning, capturing them on programme boards with named owners for each dependency. SAFe visualizes dependencies on programme boards, LeSS eliminates them through feature teams, and Nexus uses cross-team refinement, with resolution strategies including elimination through restructuring, mitigation through pre-positioning, and network analysis of transitive cascade risks.

activities.name: Plan and Execute Tranches
activities.description: Structure programme delivery into progressive capability waves with exit criteria and learning objectives.

narratives.name: Structuring Delivery Waves That Balance Ambition with Organizational Capacity
narratives.description: How to structure delivery into progressive tranches balancing ambition with absorption capacity.

narrativeContexts.context: Tranche planning requires a programme roadmap with strategic direction, an understanding of organizational change capacity, and governance authority to approve tranche boundaries and exit criteria.

MSP defines tranches as project groups structured around step changes in capability and benefit delivery, where tranche scope balances delivery rate with organizational absorption capacity. Programme increment planning provides delivery cadence within each tranche, and tranche review assesses exit criteria, benefit realization, and organizational change readiness to inform future tranche design.

activities.name: Establish Programme Governance
activities.description: Define and operationalize the governance framework including decision authorities and oversight mechanisms.

narratives.name: Building Decision Architecture That Enables Both Assurance and Agility
narratives.description: How to build governance decision architecture that enables assurance while supporting agility.

narrativeContexts.context: Programme governance design requires clarity on organizational governance structures, programme scope, and the desired balance between strategic oversight and team-level decision-making autonomy.

MSP provides governance through nine continuous themes, PMI identifies five performance domains, and Flight Levels distinguishes three decision levels preventing strategic decisions from entering operational meetings. The governance framework specifies bodies, reporting, escalation, stage gates, and risk governance while remaining lightweight enough to support rather than impede delivery.

citationNames: The Standard for Program Management, 4th Edition

activities.name: Conduct Programme Reviews
activities.description: Facilitate governance reviews assessing programme health, strategic alignment, and benefit realization.

narratives.name: Driving Data-Informed Governance Decisions Across the Programme Lifecycle
narratives.description: How to conduct data-informed governance reviews that drive effective programme decisions.

narrativeContexts.context: Reviews are scheduled at multiple cadences aligned to programme increment boundaries, tranche decision gates, and ad hoc triggers, with clear agendas covering delivery progress, strategic alignment, benefit realization, risk posture, and resource utilization.

SAFe's Inspect and Adapt combines quantitative assessment of planned versus actual objectives with structured problem-solving, while MSP's governance reviews assess whether the programme should continue, be modified, or be closed at tranche boundaries.

Reviews are data-driven using dashboard metrics, trend analysis, and comparative performance data rather than relying solely on status reports, with Flight Levels emphasizing that Level 2 and 3 reviews focus on flow and strategic alignment.

Review outputs produce governance decisions documented with rationale, improvement actions prioritized in subsequent increment backlogs, and roadmap adjustments informed by tranche outcomes and emerging strategic changes.

activities.name: Manage Programme Risk
activities.description: Identify, assess, and manage risks at programme level spanning project boundaries.

narratives.name: Managing Systemic Risk Across Programme Project Boundaries
narratives.description: How to manage systemic programme risks that span project boundaries and affect strategic objectives.

narrativeContexts.context: Programme risk management requires an established dependency register, active governance channels for escalation, and an understanding of cross-project integration points where risk cascades are most likely.

Programme-level risk management addresses strategic, integration, dependency, and governance risks spanning project boundaries through continuous identification at planning events, coordination meetings, and governance reviews. SAFe uses the ROAM framework at PI level while MSP treats risk as a continuous governance theme, with dependency register network analysis identifying cascade points and agile approaches emphasizing early delivery as primary risk mitigation.

activities.name: Optimize Dependency Practices
activities.description: Refine dependency management to enable predictive identification and automated tracking.

narratives.name: Evolving from Reactive Tracking to Predictive Dependency Intelligence
narratives.description: How dependency management evolves from reactive tracking to predictive intelligence.

narrativeContexts.context: As the programme matures through multiple tranches, the dependency register accumulates historical data on dependency patterns, resolution times, and structural causes.
Without deliberate investment in analysing patterns and automating tracking, dependency management remains a manual overhead that does not improve with experience.

The programme invests in predictive analytics that use historical patterns to identify likely dependencies before they materialize, automated tracking that reduces manual overhead, and documented practices that become organizational assets for future programmes.

activities.name: Transition Governance and Coordination
activities.description: Formally dissolve governance structures and transfer coordination responsibilities to operations.

narratives.name: Winding Down Programme Coordination While Preserving Organizational Learning
narratives.description: How to formally dissolve programme coordination while preserving organizational learning.

narrativeContexts.context: Governance transition requires that programme benefits are substantially realized or formally transferred to operational owners, final tranche reviews are complete, and governance bodies have documented their practices and lessons.

Governance dissolution transfers residual oversight to operational management, documents practices and lessons as organizational standards, delivers final reports to leadership, and preserves coordination assets including dependency management approaches and tranche planning templates as reusable institutional knowledge.

citationNames: The Standard for Program Management, 4th Edition

patterns.name: Programme Governance and Coordination Journey
patterns.description: Coordinated progression from dependency identification through tranche delivery to programme closure.

patternViews.name: Prerequisites
patternViews.description: Programme defined, governance mandated, dependencies surfaced, tranche scoped.

narrativeContexts.context: The programme has been formally defined with governance principles mandated, initial cross-project dependencies surfaced through programme board analysis, and the first tranche scoped with exit criteria and learning objectives. Governance bodies are constituted and the dependency register is established as a living tracking instrument.

patternViews.name: Governance Establishment
patternViews.description: Governance operating, dependencies analyzed, first tranche mobilized.

narrativeContexts.context: Governance structures are actively functioning with regular reviews, decision processes, and risk management operating at mandated cadence. Dependencies have been risk-assessed with resolution strategies assigned, and the first tranche is mobilized with constituent projects initiated, resources allocated, and cross-project coordination mechanisms established.

patternViews.name: Coordinated Delivery
patternViews.description: Dependencies managed, tranche delivering, governance driving decisions.

narrativeContexts.context: The programme is in active coordinated delivery with dependency resolution strategies executing, tranche progress tracked against milestones, and governance driving data-informed decisions. Programme-level risks spanning project boundaries are assessed for cascade effects, and governance reviews assess delivery progress, strategic alignment, and benefit emergence using metrics and trend analysis rather than status reports alone.

patternViews.name: Tranche Transition
patternViews.description: Dependencies minimized, tranche reviewed, capabilities transitioning.

narrativeContexts.context: The tranche is reviewed against exit criteria with benefit realization measured against targets and lessons captured. Cross-project dependencies have been minimized through structural changes including team topology alignment, architectural decoupling, and feature team adoption. The roadmap adapts based on tranche outcomes and emerging strategic changes, with governance providing optimized assurance through streamlined processes.

patternViews.name: Programme Maturation
patternViews.description: Dependencies optimized, governance transitioning, programme closing.

narrativeContexts.context: The programme achieves maturation with dependency management operating predictively using historical patterns and automated tracking, governance structures transitioning to operational management with practices documented as organizational standards, and tranche capabilities formally transitioned to operational ownership. The roadmap is fulfilled with all major capability milestones achieved, and the programme formally closes with benefits confirmed, governance dissolved, and organizational learning captured.
